accuracy_note: value_bits is a canonical encoding or fixed-bit pattern; mask_bits marks fixed bits. Zero mask bits are operand-variable fields. Chimera-native encodings are project-defined. The current instruction rows are a partial catalog of verified forms, not an exhaustive enumeration of every instruction, extension, CPU model, or encoding variant. A target is compiler-supported only for forms implemented by the encoder/decoder and backend; catalog presence alone does not imply complete executable support. Internet research update 2026-10-08: additions are sourced from the official ISA specifications listed in sources; this remains a partial catalog and each encoding must be verified against the referenced architecture manual before use in an executable encoder/decoder. Inventory update 2026-10-09: added a broad architecture-family inventory covering historical, current, embedded, vector, GPU, and virtual ISAs. Rows marked catalog-only are discovery targets and have zero verified instruction forms; the inventory is intentionally not represented as literally exhaustive, and does not imply encoder, decoder, simulator, or hardware support. GPU/VM/extension entries are explicitly distinguished from general-purpose CPU base ISAs. Execution-candidate update: execution_model lists per-architecture and per-instruction candidates with encoding, mapping, compatibility, binary-format and conformance metadata. Reference-interpreter support is limited to explicitly implemented integer operations and does not imply complete native CPU execution. Update 2026-10-11: appended additional candidate architecture and extension inventory rows from the project's curated source registry. New rows with zero instruction forms are discovery/training candidates only; no encoding, decode, execution, or conformance support is implied. AI-assisted mapping must cite database row/source references and report uncertainty; only deterministic, validated backends may execute instructions.

research_update.method: Official vendor and standards documentation reviewed for architecture scope, instruction reference organization, and extension/version status. Curated reference supplement; not exhaustive. Candidate inventory additions recorded as catalog-only unless existing source-backed instruction forms are present; no external source is treated as proof of implementation.

source_findings.finding: Intel SDM separates basic architecture, the full A–Z instruction reference, system programming (memory management, protection, interrupts/exceptions, multiprocessor, VMX/VT, SGX), and model-specific registers. Track extension and processor feature availability separately.
An ISA specifies programmer-visible instructions, formats, registers, data types, memory model, privilege, and exceptions; distinguish ISA from microarchitecture.

Track AArch64/A64 separately from AArch32 A32 and T32 (Thumb/Thumb-2); A64 is fixed 32-bit while T32 uses 16- and 32-bit encodings. Feature availability depends on architecture profile/version and implemented extensions.

RISC-V is modular: record base ISA, extensions, privileged architecture, and ratification status independently. Compressed C instructions use 16-bit encodings; base instructions commonly use 32 bits. The ratified library contains extensions beyond M/A/F/D/C/V.
Power ISA 3.1c defines user, virtual-environment, and operating-environment architecture in separate books; distinguish ISA instructions from platform requirements.

candidate_inventory_update.policy: inventory-only unless instruction forms and versioned source citations are present

candidate_inventory_sources.note: Vendor/specification landing pages are discovery provenance only. Candidate rows remain catalog-only until versioned architecture manuals or machine-readable specifications verify instruction forms.

isa_inventory_policy.scope: Broad discoverable inventory of major CISC, RISC, EPIC/VLIW, GPU, virtual-machine and extension ISAs; not a claim that every proprietary, unpublished, historical, or custom ISA is enumerated. Additional candidates now include embedded MCU/DSP/soft-core, legacy workstation/mainframe, virtual bytecode, GPU intermediate/machine ISA, and newer extension families.

status_semantics.standard: Existing architecture-level designation; verify version/profile applicability
status_semantics.legacy/standard: Legacy family with published architectural variants
status_semantics.catalog-only: Inventory/source target only; no instruction forms asserted
status_semantics.project-defined: Defined by Chimera II OS project

isa_inventory_policy.verification_rule: Instruction rows must be added only from a versioned authoritative reference or validated machine-readable definition. TableGen identifiers and family names are discovery candidates, not automatically architectural mnemonics or conformance evidence.

execution_model.policy: Discovery candidates are not conformance claims. Only explicitly implemented operations execute in the reference interpreter.

modes.native: Maps supported guest operations to Chimera semantic micro-ops; this is not native machine-code JIT output.
modes.compatibility: Interprets supported integer operations using deterministic reference semantics; unsupported operations fail closed.

elf.description: ELF object/executable; validate class, endian, machine, sections, relocations and ABI

pe-coff.description: PE/COFF object/executable; validate machine type, headers, sections, imports and relocations

mach-o.description: Mach-O object/executable; validate CPU type, file type, load commands and ABI

raw.description: Raw instruction bytes; architecture and entry point must be supplied externally

ncb.description: Chimera Native Code Binary; project-defined format requiring versioned header and loader validation

wasm.description: WebAssembly virtual ISA module; requires a sandboxed WebAssembly runtime

hosted_compatibility_modes.policy: These rows map host OS modes to physical ISA inventory candidates. A match does not mean the guest ABI, compiler backend, binary loader, or emulator is implemented. 32-bit host support applies only to matching-bitness user-space bridge and compatible host tools; it does not enable a 64-bit guest or kernel on a 32-bit host.

windows.execution: host-native matching-bitness process execution; guest PE execution still requires a validated PE runtime

linux.execution: host-native process execution; no syscall emulation

unix.execution: host-native process execution; BSD extensions remain host-dependent

macos.execution: 64-bit host-native process execution only; 32-bit macOS excluded

ai_isa_mapping.purpose: Rank candidate target instruction forms for a source operation while preserving source ISA, source provenance, compatibility constraints, and native Chimera mappings.
ai_isa_mapping.policy: Never infer executable support from architecture inventory alone. Require verified instruction forms, feature/profile checks, ABI/runtime availability, and a validated backend. AI suggestions are advisory until deterministic validation succeeds.
